tools.name: browser_status
tools.description: Check the shared browser connection without opening Chrome or showing prompts.

tools.name: browser_pages
tools.description: Find your current working pages after a conversation resumes. Recover an orphaned human handoff with browser_resume; with guardrails full, only after explicit owner confirmation.

tools.name: browser_connect
tools.description: Wait up to 10 s for the phantab bridge extension in the configured everyday Chrome profile and report the connection. Never shows a prompt; other tools wait for the bridge themselves, so this is not a required first step. profile asks about another Chrome profile the owner allowed, by its name or folder; a closed one starts without a window first, which can take up to 15 s.

tools.name: browser_open
tools.description: Open an independent invisible page sharing the owner Chrome login by default. visible explicitly opens a normal owner tab. isolated-headless has separate login. Does not control existing tabs. With snapshot true, the result ends with the new page's snapshot, as browser_snapshot shows it, so opening a page and reading it is one call. profile opens it in another Chrome profile the owner allowed, by its name or folder (default: the everyday one); a closed one starts without a window.

tools.name: browser_tabs
tools.description: List available existing website tabs with stable IDs; no focus changes. Use only when the task needs an existing owner tab. profile lists another allowed Chrome profile's tabs.

tools.name: browser_attach
tools.description: Attach to the exact existing tab requested by the owner. Never choose merely by matching a domain when multiple tabs exist. profile names the allowed Chrome profile the tab is in.

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: Read a page: its text and the controls a person could use, through open shadow roots and website frames. The result is one JSON line of page fields, then a line per control after CONTROLS: x,y for the click_xy action, tag#id, name=, type=, its text in quotes, a link's href (only its #part when it goes to a place on this page), then flags; offscreen means scroll to it first. A selector reaches the main document, then each website frame (fN, frame N of the FRAMES line, or a same-site frame, which has no mark); a control marked shadow takes click_xy instead. The page text comes last, after TEXT:. framesUnread above 0 means some frames did not answer in time, so read again. framesSkipped and elementsOmitted count what the size limits left out. With guardrails parity (the default) a text field shows what it holds as value=, except a password field or any field of a form that holds a new password, a card field, a code field or two password fields; with guardrails light or full no value is read. A ticked box or radio shows checked and a select its chosen option as selected=; text the page displays is read, including editable areas. A repeat snapshot of a page shows only the controls and text lines changed since your last one, when that is shorter, and every result leaves out page fields unchanged since your last one for that page; full true shows everything. With path, an absolute file path, the whole snapshot is saved there as JSON and the result is the path and its size in bytes, not the snapshot; an existing file is replaced only with overwrite true, and the folder must exist. Leave pageId out for the page your last call named.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Capture the assigned page for visual inspection: the view as JPEG unless format is png. fullPage true takes the whole page; selector takes one element, found as browser_act finds one (the main document, then each website frame, open shadow roots included); width and height set the view's size in CSS pixels for this picture alone (390 for a phone), and the view is put back afterwards. On a page handed to the owner (browser_show) the view is his window: fullPage, selector, width and height are refused there until handback; the plain picture is not. With path, an absolute file path, the image is saved there and the result is the path, its size in bytes and pixels, not the image; an existing file is replaced only with overwrite true, and the folder must exist. A .png path with no format saves PNG. Leave pageId out for the page your last call named.

tools.name: browser_wait
tools.description: Wait for a CSS selector or visible text in the assigned page without stealing focus; or, with only seconds (up to 60), just pause. With verification true, wait instead for the page's verification check to reach the owner or end (up to seconds, at most 60): its verification.state says how, and its next says what to do; while the owner has it, verification.wake is a command to start in the background before you end your turn, which exits once the check ends. Leave pageId out for the page your last call named.

tools.name: browser_act
tools.description: Interact with your assigned page. steps lists the actions to do, in order, each a list: ["click", selector], ["fill", selector, text], ["select", selector, value or label], ["press", key], ["type", text] (typed at the focus, as after a click_xy on a field), ["scroll", deltaY], ["click_xy", x, y] or ["navigate", url]. A selector finds its element in the main document, then in each website frame. The first that fails stops the rest and says which, and the result ends with the page's snapshot after them, or after the failure, as browser_snapshot shows it (snapshot false leaves it out), so a run of steps and its check is one call. action with its fields is the older form of one step, and then of the ones after it (each with this tool's fields but pageId); with them the snapshot comes only with snapshot true. A page handed to the owner (browser_show) refuses your writes until it is handed back; other pages on its site, yours or another agent's, keep working, unless the owner set siteLock exclusive (then one agent at a time changes a site). With guardrails light or full, a click, a press or a type with a line break or a space that reads as a payment or checkout, a password or two-factor change, or deleting an account or vault items is refused until you repeat it with ownerConfirmed true, set only after the owner explicitly approves that step; it covers the first step. Leave pageId out for the page your last call named.

tools.name: browser_show
tools.description: Show the exact working page to the owner and pause agent writes. Shared workspaces reveal the actual Chrome window with unsaved state intact; isolated headless pages use a local interactive view. With verification true, hand the owner the page's verification check (one reported as state widget); Phantab takes the page back by itself once it clears, and the result's verification.wake, started in the background before you end your turn, exits then so your harness wakes you. With release true, the page becomes the owner's ordinary tab for good, as when the work is done and the owner submits it: your record of it ends (it leaves browser_pages, and there is nothing to resume or close) and the tab stays open. Not for isolated-headless pages.

tools.name: browser_resume
tools.description: Resume after owner handback. For live views the owner clicks Return to agent; for ordinary visible tabs set ownerConfirmed after explicit user handback. With guardrails full, resume waits for one of those. A shared page goes back to its fixed hidden size, so coordinates read during the takeover no longer apply.

tools.name: browser_sign_in
tools.description: Sign in to the site on this page with its saved login, with no secret ever shown to you. url in place of pageId opens the page first, as browser_open does with its defaults, so opening a sign-in page and signing in is one call; the result starts with the opened page's line. Sign-in only: refuses sign-up and paying forms. Returns a status and never a secret; call again per step (next-step). Never claims signed-in: after submitted or next-step the result ends with the page's snapshot, as browser_snapshot shows it. account picks one saved login by its exact name when status is ambiguous. vault picks one of the owner's configured password managers by name; omit it to use them in the owner's order. Statuses: README.md of phantab.

tools.name: browser_sign_up
tools.description: Make the site's new password for a sign-up the owner asked for: phantab creates and saves a strong password in the owner's password manager for this site (the one vault names, else the owner's choice) and fills it into the page's new-password fields, never showing it to you. Fill the form's other fields first; then press the site's own button yourself. Returns a status, never a secret. If a check appears after submit, use browser_wait/browser_show with verification true.

tools.name: browser_close
tools.description: Close only agent-created pages; detach from owner tabs without closing them. Refuses while owner takeover is active.
